question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in continuation subsystem, including trusted cross-session delegate-return delivery, in PR #85651 after proof and conflict refresh, or require a narrower split first?
rationale: Automation can verify source and proof gaps, but it cannot decide whether trusted cross-session context injection and a large core orchestration subsystem fit the maintainer security/product boundary.

options.title: Accept after refresh
options.body: Keep PR #85651 as the canonical path, but require a clean merge result, exact-head live proof, and explicit maintainer sign-off on trusted cross-session returns before merge.

options.title: Split before merge
options.body: Ask for smaller PRs that separate config/tool registration, session-delivery substrate, compaction lifecycle, and cross-session trusted-return policy.

options.title: Pause core inclusion
options.body: Close or pause the core PR and move the idea through an RFC or plugin/API-seam path until maintainers choose a narrower architecture.

recommendation.title: Accept after refresh
recommendation.body: Keep PR #85651 as the canonical path, but require a clean merge result, exact-head live proof, and explicit maintainer sign-off on trusted cross-session returns before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent history across auto-reply, session management, system-event authority, and plugin SDK boundaries that this decision spans.
